transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in, and what concerns have you been having?

I've decided to come because I know I'm being watched and monitored, and I think people are out to get me. It's been happening constantly for about four months now, and I just don't feel safe anywhere. I had to make sure it was even safe to come here today.

During these four months, have you also had a period of feeling unusually high or energized with much less need for sleep, or a period of feeling very depressed most of the day nearly every day? If so, did those mood symptoms happen only at the same time as the feeling of being watched, or also separately?

No, I haven't experienced those periods of feeling unusually high or energized, nor have I felt severely depressed in that way. My main concern is just dealing with the fact that I'm being watched all the time.
Besides feeling watched, have you been hearing voices when no one is there, or have your thoughts or speech become confused or hard for other people to follow?

No, I don't hear any voices at all. But people around me have been complaining that my speech is hard to follow, telling me that I'm constantly jumping from one topic to another and not making any sense when I talk.
Have these problems made it hard for you to work, study, or take care of yourself, and have you noticed this has been going on for at least six months in total?

Yes, it's been very hard to work or take care of myself because I feel completely unmotivated and have withdrawn from everyone. While the most intense things like being watched have been happening for four months, I've actually been struggling with these overall issues for about two years and two months.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["Schizophrenia"], and based on this conversation the list remains the same. The patient reports a persistent persecutory delusion for 4 months, disorganized speech noted by others, marked functional decline and social withdrawal/self-care impairment, with overall disturbance lasting more than 6 months (about 2 years and 2 months). They deny manic or major depressive episodes, making schizoaffective disorder and bipolar disorder less likely, and the presence of disorganized speech and functional deterioration makes delusional disorder less likely.
